snippet:
Slave Knight Gael -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia 
 trivia : Gael's facial data, including his beard, is unique to him and is not available as an option when creating the player's character.
Impaling the corpse of a Pygmy lord with his sword and tossing it at the player is a reference to Knight Artorias, who performs a similar act at the start of his boss fight, and to the Penetrator before him in *Demon's Souls*.
Out of any boss from the entire franchise, Gael has the biggest boss arena, as the Pygmy's Throne is a completely explorable desert-like zone.
The way Gael moves and fights on the first phase is very similar to how Guts, from the *Berserk* anime/manga, does when using the Berserker Armor. In the second phase, the Repeating Crossbow is also reminiscent of Guts' Repeater Crossbow and the way he hides and follows his attacks with a cape.
A summon sign appears beneath Gael wherever he reappears at when he teleports during his boss fight.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
If the Ashen One chooses to ignore Friede and explores the Painted World, they may fight the Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf, which allows the Ashen One to participate in the Undead Match. Deeper inside the painting, the Ashen One finds the Painter, Slave Knight Gael's aforementioned Lady, who has been imprisoned by Friede and Vilhelm in order to prevent her from painting the next world. If the Ashen One opens the way to the inner sanctum hiding Father Ariandel, Friede will confront them and fight to preserve the painting. After a long battle, the Ashen One defeats Friede and Ariandel, prompting the Painted World to begin burning and dooming it to destruction.

The Painter informs the Ashen One that she has sent Gael to find the Dark Soul, which she will use for her next painting.

title: Humans
snippet: On their quest, the Ashen One encounters the Painted World of Ariandel, and a little girl whose duty it is to become the new Painter, and replace it with a fresh, unrotted version. To do this, she reveals that she needs the blood of the bearer of the Dark Soul, and that her guardian Gael has gone to find it. At the end of time, as the flames are reduced to embers and sparks, the entire world has begun to collapse in on itself, surrounding the ageless Ringed City. Gael travels to this heap of reality to find the Dark Soul, with the Ashen One following suit, eventually slaying Argo, the leader of the Spears of the Church.

title: Furtive Pygmy
snippet:
Sometime before the arrival of the Ashen One at the Ringed City, a pygmy—plausibly a disgruntled Pygmy Lord— came to detest the Gods for condemning the pygmies to their accursed fate, and took up residence at the outskirts of their city. There, he welcomed new arrivals and directed into Filianore's Church those who sought the Dark Soul, where they could confront the "lid covering an overgrown privy".

The Pygmy Lords obeyed and relied on the gods for eons, and remained passive unto the end of time, at which point even their own blood had dried up. The last Pygmy Lords would meet their ends at the hands of Slave Knight Gael, who had sought their Dark Soul for centuries. Finding that their blood had long ago dried up, he consumed their Dark Soul, so that he could take it back to his Lady to be used as pigment for her painting.

title: Slave Knight Gael
snippet:
Slave Knight Gael -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Gael was once a slave knight, an order of Undead knights who were used as fodder in the bleakest of battles. Even as they grew decrepit, their skin charred black, their bones twisted and their minds lost, they were never relieved from duty, their condemned stature signified by their vibrant red hoods. At one point, Gael managed to free himself from his life of bloody battles and ended up in the Painted World of Ariandel, a refuge for the forlorn souls who had no place to call home. There he eventually met the Painter, the "Lady" of the corvian inhabitants of the Painted World, who had extensive knowledge of the First Flame and the Dark Soul. The Painter apparently had the ability to incorporate these two concepts into creating new Painted Worlds. Gael eventually came to be a parental figure for her, such that she called him "Uncle Gael".

He also warns them to suppress their curiosity, as the depths of the painting would easily destroy them in their endeavors to sate it.

When encountered in the building housing the captive painter girl, he will deride the Ashen One's inquisitiveness, claiming he has seen their type often and that they would never have what it takes to actually face the danger they have put themselves in by sticking their nose where it didn't belong. After a duel to the death, the Unkindled champion is victorious, slaying Vilhelm, who laments his failure to uphold his oath to Friede.

title: Dark Soul
snippet: Near the end of the Age of Fire, a slave knight called Gael traveled to the Ringed City, seeking the Pygmy Lords to gain their blood. The blood of the Dark Soul was intended to be used to paint a new Painted World, but to Gael's shock, Filianore's spell was broken and the Pygmy Lords were aged to the point that their blood did not flow, for it was dried in their veins. Even though he knew he had not the strength to survive bearing it, Gael slew the Pygmy Lords and drank from their wounds, absorbing the Dark Soul into himself. It imbued him with a dark miasma and warped his mind, but in the end he was successful, slain by the Ashen One to extract the soul's blood. The current state of the Dark Soul is unknown, but given the eternal nature of Lord Souls, it is unlikely that it was truly destroyed.

title: Slave Knight Gael
snippet: Gael's mission was therefore not over, and so the knight set off again with a new mission: to find the Dark Soul and bring it back to the Painter so she could complete her painting. He knew that he lacked a Champion's strength, that bearing the Dark Soul would likely ruin and consume him, leaving him scant hope of safe return; nonetheless, he set out on his endless journey, crossing the centuries through countless battles and hardships. His Executioner's Greatsword remained with him from beginning to end, becoming heavily chipped and stained with blood, and the Repeating Crossbow he customized was rusted with blood, overused, twisted and marred with dents and scratches. Gael's own body too suffered from the long journey, being consumed by the ever-expanding Darksign that fused his flesh with his now rusted and cracked armor.

It's possible that Slave Knight Gael was once such a believer, due to his usage of that very miracle. That is in spite of his nature as a cursed Undead, which the old god seemingly despised.

title: Dark Soul
snippet:
Dark Soul -  Dark Souls - item - lore 
 lore : During the advent of Fire, the concept of Disparity came into existence, and with it the Dark and the Light. At some point humanoid creatures found powerful souls near the First Flame and claimed them, becoming known as Lords. While the other three "Lords" found larger souls, a lowly and forgotten being known only as the Furtive Pygmy found a fourth, peculiar soul: the Dark Soul.

title: Dark Soul
snippet:
Most Humans would come to serve the Gods in the years that followed, while their ancestors, the Pygmies and their royal family, were relocated to the Ringed City, “gifted” to them by the "generous" Lord Gwyn. He also gave to them his youngest daughter, Filianore, and as she was given away, her father promised the Princess that he would come back for her, one day.

Those royal pygmies that retreated to the Ringed City brought the Dark Soul with them, with the original soul eventually ending up split among multiple Pygmy Lords. The majority of the royals of the Pygmies continued to serve and revere the gods for millennia, but the Ringed Knights that took parts in the ancient war against the dragons subtly defied them in what ways they could.

title: Dark Soul
snippet:
Dark Soul -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : The Dark Soul, one of the unique Lord Souls, was claimed by the Furtive Pygmy, the ancestor of the Chosen Undead and Humanity. In the introduction to the first *Dark Souls*, it is depicted as a small, reddish flame like a candle. However, this conflicts with later descriptions.

title: Dark Soul
snippet: In terms of passive uses, bearers or close descendants of the true Dark Soul via its Blood—such as the Pygmies—have increased longevity, though it does not seem to truly render mortal bearers immune to age and death. It is discovered that the Dark Soul carries the power necessary to create a Painted World, and the painter of the next incarnation uses this "pigment" to paint a cold, dark world on a canvas to escape the current painted world, once two Unkindled (Elfriede & the Ashen One) arrive and ignite the flame that burns its rot away.

title: Dark Soul
snippet:
Dark Soul -  Dark Souls - item - capabilities 
 capabilities : Any fragment of the Dark Soul that separates from the original can be fueled by emotions and willpower, and increase its usable power, making it the most unique of the four Lord Souls.

Most notable of its functions is the power to animate life and raise sentient beings from the Abyss, for the Dark Soul is the only Lord Soul which is intrinsically tied to the Abyss, unlike the other forms of life that take energy from Souls. The main lifeform connected to it is the Human race, but lesser creatures are said to have also risen from the Dark, such as the White-faced Locust. The Dark Soul is also linked to the Dark Hand, and by extension, the art of Lifedrain. This is the legendary power of the fabled Dark Lord, used to gain humanity from others. The Darkwraiths used this power to steal Humanity from their victims.

title: Dark Soul
snippet: Using the Dark Soul, the Pygmy created black sprites of darkness called Humanity, which was given to his descendants. These dark-souled beings risen from the Abyss were called Humans, and each bore a small fragment of the Dark Soul. When the other Lords began fighting against the Everlasting Dragons, they conscripted the Humans into the forces, who aided the Lords by forging quasi-living arms and armor deep within the Abyss. But the Humans were betrayed by the Lords, for they feared the Dark that resides within each and every one of them. Their contributions to the War of the Ancients went completely unrecorded, and upon their Humanity, the Gods placed a sealing ring of fire, later to be known as the Darksign.

title: Filianore
snippet:
Filianore -  Dark Souls III - character - theories 
 theories : Given that her name doesn't contain the particle "Gwyn" like her siblings, it is possible to theorize that Gwyn wholly severed kinship ties with Filianore as he "gave" her away. Doing so could have served to impede a Pygmy Lord being officially inducted into the Anor Londo clan through marriage with Filianore, in the same way as it had happened with Seath the Scaleless, a prospect which Gwyn likely desired to avoid, given the Pygmies' heritage. If so, Gwyn's "gift" of his daughter to the Pygmies would be a merely symbolic gesture with little political value. Furthermore, her title as "Princess" seems to indicate that she never married into the pygmy royalty.

title: Filianore
snippet:
Filianore -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Filianore is the last daughter of Gwyn, Lord of Sunlight. Her sacred symbol is a crest of young grass.

She did not reside in Anor Londo during the Age of Fire unlike the other deities. Her father Gwyn, after winning the war against the dragons, "gave" Filianore as a gift to the Pygmy Lords together with a magnificent ringed city at the edge of the world. Before leaving her in the Ringed City, Gwyn promised her that he would come back for her some day.

Throughout the millennia that followed in the Age of Fire, the Pygmies worshipped Filianore as a goddess, building a church in her name with her as the matriarch. Even the Pygmy Lords who possessed the Dark Soul and ruled the city relied on her for salvation.

title: Filianore
snippet: At a certain point Filianore fell into a deep sleep hugging a Vagrant egg, causing the appearance of a space-time barrier that isolated the Ringed City from the effects of the fading of the First Flame on the rest of the world. The order of the Spears of the Church was thus founded, which enlisted knights with the duty of protecting the princess's slumber from trespassers, and maintaining the city's state of isolation and containing the Dark Soul within. These guardians received Filianore's Spear Ornaments as proof of the fulfillment of their duties.

title: Filianore

title: First sin
snippet: The term "First Sin" is likely derived from the Judeo-Christian account of humankind's [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Original_sin original sin], generally agreed amongst most sects to be a base flaw in all people stemming from the original humans, Adam and Eve, partaking in the fruits of a certain tree in the Garden of Eden; the sole action God strictly forbade that they do under threat of death. This fruit opened their eyes, allowing them to see and "be as God, knowing good and evil", but in disobeying God they effectively caused humans to be branded by Him as untrustworthy and capable of sin. He then cast them out of the Garden and had them toil for their food all their lives. Most significantly, however, was that there was a second tree within the Garden that bestowed everlasting life, with God Himself saying "and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever" before casting the pair out to eventually die.

All he is missing is their signature crown, something that was seemingly gifted to them by Gwyn and the Gods, which he very openly despises.

He believes that the Ashen One found their way to the city in an attempt to dispell Filianore's illusion and get their hands on the Dark Soul, no matter what they say about their own intentions. He directs them to the ends of the city, claiming to be their friend and ally and vanishing once the deed is done.

snippet:
Shira, Knight of Filianore -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : is a character and summonable phantom in the *Dark Souls III: The Ringed City DLC*. At a certain stage of the DLC, she will permanently turn hostile.

She is voiced by Poppy Drayton.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet:
Shira, Knight of Filianore -  Dark Souls III - character - plot 
 plot : Shira is one of the few friendly characters in the Ringed City. She stands behind a locked door and can be interacted from the other side. Upon telling her the name of Lord Gwyn she will warm up to the player's presence, and request of them the great favor of mercy-killing the afflicted Midir, a dragon that still guards the city and the princess from intruders. If the player accepts to aid her, she will give them the Sacred Chime of Filianore.

This interaction will also allow Shira to be summoned for the boss fight against said dragon, providing ranged support with her Lightning Arrow miracle. She tends to have a hard time keeping up with the beast's aggressive attacks however. Summoning her for the encounter or not has no bearing on the completion of her request, as she'll thank the player for granting Midir his deserved rest regardless. As a reward, she'll give out a Titanite Slab.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet:
Shira, Knight of Filianore -  Dark Souls III - character - theories 
 theories : It is incredibly likely that the Duke mentioned by Shira is none other than Seath the Scaleless himself. For one, he is the only prominent duke who is ever mentioned as part of the age of the gods, which would explain why Shira speaks of her parentage to a duke as if it were self-explanatory. Another clue may come from the pearl lodged in her crown, which was harvested from the Man Eater Clams. These creatures were found nesting in the Crystal Cave, part of Seath's domain, as well as the primordial Ash Lake, a place tied to the dragons.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet:
Shira, Knight of Filianore -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia 
 trivia : Shira's Japanese name "**シラ**" could also be read as an alternative spelling of "Scylla", which is the name of a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scylla sea monster] in Greek mythology.
**This could lend more credence to her connection to Seath, as the Japanese name for the Pisacas, some of his creations, is the more widely used Japanese name for Scylla: "**スキュラ**".
Her concept art shows her with flowing white hair, while her in-game model opts for light brown hair, bordering dirty blonde, tied up in a braid.
Due to a bug in the PC version, she may clip through the floor and fall to her death when she is summoned, or traverse the fog before the beginning of Darkeater Midir's boss fight.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet: The Lord of Sunlight would end up gifting the Pygmies with a magnificent city at the edge of the world, sealing the deal by relinquishing his beloved daughter too, who would remain there until the day he would return for her. Shira and her trusted friend, the dragon Midir, who was raised by the Gods and given the duty of battling the Dark, would follow their liege and guard the Ringed City, keeping those who would rouse her awake at bay. By the king's decree, the Judicator Giants and the Spears of the Church would follow suit, ensuring peace. Shira seemes to admire this order, especially those of them who would reach the rank of Divine Spear.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet: Shira and Midir continued to uphold their duties, even as the state of the city deteriorated over the countless years of the unnaturally prolonged Age of Fire. Even as the world began collapsing onto itself, the two stood dutiful, until the Ashen One follows the path of the world-ending spiral to the hidden city. The Unkindled, speaking the name of the ancient king Gwyn, manages to win the knight's trust, who takes the opportunity to enlist them to finally put Midir to rest, even offering her aid to accomplish that feat, leaving the darkroom she had secluded herself into just for the sake of releasing her friend from his duties.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet: Shira would eventually have to quell a corruption that had been growing within the very city, caused by a mad king that had emerged among the other Pygmy Lords. When she tried to put him to rest, she realized that his body could not die, and he simply remained impaled to her cross spear, which began to be permeated with the king's dark power. As a result, Shira would bring her weapon to a darkroom, sealing the door shut and remaining by its side to ensure the king would remain put. Even in this prolonged captivity, the descendant of the Gods remained dignified, wearing her noble attire even though no one would see it.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet:
Shira, Knight of Filianore -  Dark Souls III - character - strategy 
 strategy : Shira is likely to be the player's final NPC fight in the game, and as such she proves to be fairly challenging. She'll constantly cast Lightning Arrow against players who stay out of reach of her halberd. Sometimes she'll even be the one to create distance on purpose so she may safely attack them from a distance.

She favors using her melee weapon two-handed when it's time to fight at close range, and she isn't shy about using her weapon's Mad King's Folly skill either. It allows her to gain a temporary buff to her poise and defense, cast a dark projectile, or simply hit the player with a screech which knocks them back a fair bit, so that she may begin pelting them with elemental arrows again.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet: She has access to five Estus Flasks during this encounter, allowing her to persist much longer than other enemies like her. Her resistence to Fire and Lightning is also nothing to scoff at. Thankfully she remains susceptible to status effects like Poison/Toxic and Frost, which could help greatly during the battle. Luring her away to the single Ringed Knight who resides within the ashen wasteland is not a good idea however, as the enemy will not be hostile to Shira and will instead work with her to destroy the player.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet:
Even the name has some thematic and etymological connection to Seath, as Shira resembles the Japanese word for "white", written as "**白**" and pronounced "*shiro*", a kanji that makes up part of the Duke's title of "White Dragon", written as "**白竜**". It doesn't stop there, though, as the name also shares an impressive connection with Priscilla's, as Shira's Japanese name "**シラ**" is part of the Crossbreed's Japanese name "**プリシラ**". Priscilla's connections to Seath come from her stark white coloration and her nature as a half-dragon, as crossbreeds were something the old Paledrake was highly interested in. This would make the two half-sisters, but not full ones, as Priscilla is stated to have been born of adultery, meaning they'd have two distinct mothers.

This is all just speculation, however, to be taken with a grain of salt.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet: Meanwhile, her friend Midir had been corroded by the powers of the Dark he had been battling. Although his strong sense of duty wouldn't let him cease his watch, the knight reluctantly concluded that the afflicted dragon had to die, for the Dark would eventually destroy everything that made him who he was, eroding him into nothing but a mad beast. She wished to let him pass on with his honor and sense of self still intact.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet: The great weight lifted from Midir's shoulders is celebrated, but the respite is brief. In truth, the Ashen One was seeking Princess Filianore, following the trail that had been left by Gael. This was the one thing Shira had warned them not to do. Betrayed and filled with righteous fury, she attacks the Unkindled in the name of her heritage, her princess and her companion Midir. The champion of Ash would triumph, likely extinguishing the line of the Gods.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet:
Shira, Knight of Filianore -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : Shira is a descendant of the Gods, a child of royalty, and the daughter of a certain Duke, who goes unnamed. Her crown denotes her noble pedigree, made out of silver and adorned with a pearl retrieved from a dangerous Man Eater Shell. She appears to have been from the early age of the gods, as she makes use of a miracle of that era, issued to female knights. She was also the sworn knight and personal handmaiden of Princess Filianore, the youngest daughter of Gwyn.

title: Shira, Knight of Filianore
snippet: Shira's descent from royalty and the Gods would also make sense, due to the original *Dark Souls* establishing that Seath had become part of Gwyn's family by becoming the consort of one of his female relatives. This would mean that she would be born of that marriage, thus retaining most of her divine heritage. Her friendship with Midir could also take on a new light, as if she had draconic descent, she'd be able to relate and even grow incredibly close to the great being with relative ease due to their partially shared roots.

title: Slave Knight Gael
snippet: fight_overview : When encountered as a boss, Gael appears monstrous and his moves mirror his beastly nature, he does high amounts of damage and can endure some significant punishment himself. Aside from the damage his moveset has him bounding, and jumping around the players position in a manner that can even force the lock-on function to drop. His attacks are all easy to memorize however, and the only time the player should worry is when Gael rears back, releases a frustrated groan, quickly followed by several powerful strikes. Followed at the end by high leap plunge attack that affects a small area around the blades impact. Key to this battle is his poise, he can be staggered but not riposted, the player should pay close attention to how many hits it takes to stagger him (usually three with great weapons), and act accordingly, if this weakness exploited correctly he can be stunned out of his hard-hitting combos in the second phase.
